belief: If doctors can't find the cause, it must be all in my head.
origins: Pain without a clear test result is common. When scans are normal, some patients are dismissed, and many begin to doubt themselves. Self-doubt can lead to shame, silence, and stopping the search for help.
teaches: Jesus took seriously the suffering of the woman with bleeding who had spent everything on doctors and was no better, and He said, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction” (Mark 5:34). Pain is real whether or not it appears on a test. Scripture says, “I am weary from groaning” (Psalm 6:6) and “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” God is a compassionate Father who believes you, even when others struggle to. Keep seeking help, because medicine does not know everything.
self_statements: No test shows anything, so I am imagining it.
The doctors are right and I am wrong.
errors: Believing pain is either visible on tests or imaginary.
Predicting that no one will ever believe me.
Feeling dismissed and concluding I am imagining it.
questions: What do I know about my pain from my own experience?
Who has believed me and taken me seriously?
What have I not yet tried, such as a pain specialist or a second opinion?
What do I want to say to my care team?
What does Jesus’ care for the suffering woman say about my pain?
Who can go to appointments with me?
truth: My pain is real, even when tests are normal. I can keep seeking help, speak plainly with my care team, and rest in a God who believes me and cares.
hw_truths: Jesus cares for those who suffer.
I can keep looking for help.
log: Each week, note one step you took to get care.
actions: List symptoms, timing, and what helps.
Take a friend to an appointment.
Ask about specialists or pain clinics.
prayer: Lord, no one can find the cause, but You know my pain. Give me persistence, wise doctors, and people who believe me. Amen.
